source.title: Solving a Real AI Engineer Take-Home Assignment

ideas.title: Do not start a vague take-home by coding
ideas.post_angle: A vague AI engineer take-home should start with scoping, assumptions, clarifying questions, and data-source choices before implementation.
ideas.why_worth_posting: This is the career lesson that frames the whole workshop and is useful to anyone interviewing for AI engineer roles.

source_moments.note: The assignment is vague, so the first step is brainstorming scope, data sources, and clarifying questions.
The implementation should be shaped by available data sources and APIs.

clip.title: Scope before coding
clip.reason: Clear opening section about handling an underspecified take-home assignment.
clip.trim_notes: Start when the assignment is introduced; end after the data-source framing.

ideas.writing_brief: Write a post about how to approach vague AI engineer take-home assignments before writing code.

ideas.title: Build the CLI before the Telegram bot
ideas.post_angle: For an agent product, start with a simple terminal app before adding UI or Telegram because it makes the core loop easier to inspect.
ideas.why_worth_posting: This is a tactical engineering pattern that applies to many agent projects, not only this assignment.

source_moments.note: Instead of starting with Telegram, the workshop starts with a terminal app and adds Telegram later.
The CLI makes it possible to inspect tool use and improve answer structure.

clip.title: CLI first, Telegram later
clip.reason: Short, clear explanation of why the implementation starts with the terminal.
clip.trim_notes: Keep the Python/UV setup if it helps the flow.

ideas.writing_brief: Write a post about reducing agent-project risk by building the core interaction in a CLI first.

ideas.title: Pointless tests are worse than no signal
ideas.post_angle: Agent-generated tests often assert imports, names, or prompt wording instead of behavior, so the engineer needs to delete and rewrite them.
ideas.why_worth_posting: The transcript has an unusually concrete and opinionated testing lesson that many AI-assisted developers will recognize.

source_moments.note: The generated tests are called pointless because they test imports and method names, not behavior.
Bad tests are removed and replaced with behavior-oriented agent tests.
The workshop prioritizes cleaning tests before cleaning the rest of the code.

clip.title: Delete pointless tests
clip.reason: Strongest section for a testing-focused social clip.
clip.trim_notes: Start at reviewing test_agent; end after the desired test shape is described.

ideas.writing_brief: Write a post about useful tests for AI-generated agent code and why shallow generated tests should be rewritten.

ideas.title: Evaluate both the answer and the trajectory
ideas.post_angle: Agent evaluations should check the final answer and the trajectory: which tools were called, in what order, and whether the path made sense.
ideas.why_worth_posting: This is the most technical agent-evaluation lesson in the session and turns vague eval advice into a practical pattern.

source_moments.note: The eval framework runs scenarios, judges outputs, and inspects tool-call trajectories.
The README should document scenarios, limitations, tests, and evals.

clip.title: Judge answers and trajectories
clip.reason: Compact explanation of input, expected output, judge, and trajectory evaluation.

ideas.writing_brief: Write a post about evaluating agents by checking both the final response and the sequence of tool calls.

ideas.title: The best bug came from using the bot
ideas.post_angle: A live Telegram test found that the agent could loop on a tool call, which is exactly the kind of failure that should become an eval or unit test.
ideas.why_worth_posting: It is a memorable real failure from the workshop and shows why demos and monitoring are part of engineering, not decoration.

source_moments.note: The CLI agent is wrapped as a Telegram bot and tested in Telegram.
A query makes the bot loop on search calls, so the next step is a tool-call limit and an assertion.

clip.title: The bot looped, so write the test
clip.reason: A concrete failure turns into a clear engineering follow-up.
clip.trim_notes: Start when the bot is working in monitoring; end after the five-tool-call assertion idea.

ideas.writing_brief: Write a post about turning a live agent failure into a regression test and eval scenario.

ideas.title: Your README is part of the interview
ideas.post_angle: For AI engineer take-homes and portfolio projects, a polished README can matter as much as the code because reviewers may only have a few minutes.
ideas.why_worth_posting: This is the strongest closing career takeaway and gives candidates a practical checklist.

source_moments.note: The README should explain the storyline, decisions, limitations, generated code, and follow-up work.
Hiring managers may start with the README, so it should show tests, evals, monitoring, screenshots, and next steps.

clip.title: Polish the README
clip.reason: A strong closing clip about portfolio and interview presentation.

ideas.writing_brief: Write a post about treating the README as the first interview artifact for take-home assignments.
